title: Protocol for biomimetic tumoroid models by plastic compression using centrifugation
author: Devereaux, Lam, et al.

steps.title: Prepare tumor mass
steps.instruction: Set up collagen I gel with tumor cells, solidify, and compress by centrifugation (≈1.5 h).

substeps.instruction: On ice, mix collagen I and MEM by gentle hand swirling; avoid bubbles.

Add neutralizing solution drop‑by‑drop while swirling gently until the mixture turns salmon pink (target pH ~7.2–7.4). If the color becomes hot pink, the mixture is over‑neutralized and must be remade.
Leave the mixture on ice with lids off for ~20 min to allow bubbles to escape.
Add media containing 5 × 10⁴ cells of the desired tumor line per gel (scale by the number of gels) and mix gently, avoiding bubbles.
Pipette 240 µL of the gel mixture into each central well of a 96‑well plate (do not use border wells); work with two plates in parallel for balance.
Incubate for 15 min at 37 °C to allow gelation.
Add 60 µL of culture media on top of each solidified gel.
Using sterile tweezers, gently scrape around the circumference of the well to free‑float the gel; avoid damaging it.
Centrifuge the plates at 4347 RCF (≈4500 RPM on an Eppendorf 5910 R centrifuge) for 15 min with the rotor balanced; this performs plastic compression.
Pipette off excess liquid from atop the compressed gels, leaving only the thin compressed tumor mass.

steps.title: Prepare stroma and embed tumor mass
steps.instruction: Create stromal collagen gels, place compressed tumor masses onto them, and compress the combined construct (≈1.5 h).

substeps.instruction: Prepare a collagen‑I gel mixture as described for the tumor mass, keeping it on ice; the mixture may be acellular or contain stromal cells (e.g., fibroblasts). Optionally make this gel at the same time as the 96‑well gels.
Pipette 650 µL (half the final gel volume) into each central well of a 24‑well plate (leave border wells empty); work with two plates in parallel for balance.
Incubate for 20 min at 37 °C to gel.
Using sterile tweezers, place one compressed tumor mass onto each solidified gel, then carefully add the remaining 650 µL of gel mixture on top, pipetting slowly to keep the TM centered.
Incubate the construct for 20 min at 37 °C to allow the top gel to set.
Add 1.3 mL of appropriate culture media atop each compartmentalized gel and, with sterile tweezers, lift the gel around the well edge so it becomes free‑floating.
Centrifuge at 4347 RCF for 15 min (balanced).
Remove excess liquid, leaving only the compressed tumoroid.
Add 1 mL of fresh media on top of each tumoroid.
Place plates in a cell‑culture incubator; replace 50 % of spent media with fresh media every 48 h.
Proceed with downstream experiments as required (e.g., drug treatment, immunofluorescence imaging, flow cytometry).
